description:
FILED AND FIXED s526w2 (Opus, resumed s528 2026-10-25), from the Log-Log4perl-1.58 board census (t/004Config.t rows 26-28: `open STDERR, ">$TMP_FILE"; ... close STDERR;` then a later eval's warn).  PRE-EXISTING (main 31cd8c02).

    open STDERR, ">/tmp/f"; print STDERR "x\n"; close STDERR;
    eval { warn "after close\n"; print STDERR "p\n"; 1 }; print "1 [", ($@ // ''), "]\n";
  perl 5.40.3: 1 []      PCL: 1 [#<sb-sys:fd-stream for "descriptor 2" {...}> is closed at (eval 0) line 0.]
  (`print STDERR` on the closed handle was already right: returns false.)  Probe scratch/s526w2/pstderr.pl.

=== DONE (s526w2) ===
cl/pcl-runtime.lisp p-warn: the default branch's write moves into %p-warn-to-stderr, which drops a host stream-error (a closed STDERR) -- an EFFECT-only loss with no value flowing on, perl's own answer, so not a rule-12 die.  A tied STDERR and $SIG{__WARN__} are untouched.  Guard Pl/t/misc-fixes-01.t row 143 (inverse-verified on a 31cd8c02 extraction).  Log-Log4perl t/004Config.t 21/7 -> see the board run (rows 26-28).
subject: `warn` with STDERR CLOSED died with the host's `#<sb-sys:fd-stream for "descriptor 2"> is closed` text (into $@); perl drops the warning and continues
